entries.effect: Main Menu -> Einstellungen — the height of every settings row. At ten times its shipped height the rows are absurdly tall, the dropdowns render as tall rectangles and the page layout visibly breaks.
entries.note: Export 44, object `SizeBox_SettingsEntry`, class `/Script/UMG.SizeBox`, leaf `/MinDesiredHeight`: one little-endian float32, `00002042` (40.0f) replaced by `0000c843` (400.0f). Packed as the additive Zen triplet `zzz_GoreSettingsRowTall_P` and taken into the game through `gore mgr`, which classified it as a foreign IoStore triplet — it carries no `gore-mod.json` — and applied it as `zzz_gm000_GoreSettingsRowTall_P`, because `gore asset pack` does not deploy. Before this, no edit these commands made had ever been observed to take effect in game; the workflow was trusted because the bytes and the receipts said so and for no other reason. Read the scope exactly: one asset, one leaf, one float, one build, one look, and the target was a cooked UMG widget package rather than a DataAsset proper. It says nothing about other leaf kinds, other asset classes or other builds.

entries.effect: The hero's footprint decals — their size comes from BoneData/BoneFeetData/FeetTextureSize
entries.note: Extends this domain past the one case it had. The first sighting was a UMG widget (W_SettingsRow) and a float32; this is a real native DataAsset — class /Script/G1R.FootstepTag, not a Blueprint-generated one — and the leaf is a vector4_f64x4, reached through a struct inside a struct. FeetTextureSize was raised from (16,16,0,1) to (160,160,0,1) and the footprints came out roughly ten times too large. Provenance is clean here in a way the settings-row sighting's was not: extracted, patched, packed, deployed and observed all on build 24539464. Delivered through `gore mgr` as a foreign triplet, alongside the settings-row triplet, which served as the control that the deployment had landed at all.

observations.witness: einstellungsseite absurd groß, fußabdrücke absurd groß

entries.note: Unreachable by `gore asset`, and the reason generalises. Its export is a Blueprint-generated class (BP_PostProcessDynamicData_C); the USMAP describes native classes, so there is no schema to bind and `inspect` reports status "unsupported" with zero editable leaves. Every asset whose export class ends in `_C` is in the same position. This is a tool limit, not a game one — nothing was deployed and nothing was observed in game.

observations.witness: ASSET_SCHEMA: export 0 class "…BP_PostProcessDynamicData_C" cannot be bound to USMAP: schema was not found

entries.note: A second, different reach limit. The class IS native (/Script/Engine.MaterialParameterCollection) and binds cleanly, but the walk stops at `struct "Guid" has no proven G1R UE5.4 wire form at byte 6` and the export yields no leaves. One unproven struct type therefore costs the whole export, not just the field containing it. Also a tool limit; nothing was deployed.

observations.witness: ASSET_WALK: struct "Guid" has no proven G1R UE5.4 wire form at byte 6
